title: Tigecycline versus imipenem/cilastatin for complicated intra-abdominal infection: clinical cure at test-of-cure
question: Among trials randomising adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection to tigecycline or to imipenem/cilastatin, how does the proportion cured at the test-of-cure visit compare, and does that comparison survive the choices made in reaching it?
_prose_rule: Prose may not restate a number the object holds structurally.
_sourcing_rule: Every MEASURED input carries the verbatim sentence it was read from. The one DERIVED row shows its arithmetic on itself.
_year_field_note: The year on each trial is the PUBLICATION year its PubMed record prints under PubDate. An earlier build took the first year appearing in the record, which is the indexing DateCompleted or DateRevised and sits ABOVE PubDate in the XML, so more than one trial carried a year no source asserts -- in one case a revision date years after the paper. A reviewer caught it beside the identifiers, which is exactly where a reader would read it as the study's year.
_estimand_rule: One indication, one comparator, one analysis population, one outcome. Anything that changes any of those four is a different comparison and is either excluded with a reason or held as a sensitivity analysis.
_direction_rule: Clinical cure is BENEFICIAL. A ratio below the null therefore means the intervention cured LESS often. Nothing in this object may colour or word a ratio below the null as a benefit.
completeness_statement: Every trial found that randomises this population to this intervention against this comparator AND publishes per-arm counts in the analysis population is held and pooled. One further eligible registrational trial exists whose per-arm figures are published only inside a pooled report this build could not open; it is listed as eligible and contributing no data, and it is not excluded. Trials in the other licensed indication, and cIAI trials against a different comparator, are outside the scope and are named where they are excluded rather than left unmentioned.

eligible_but_not_contributing.note: This registrational trial meets every eligibility criterion and is NOT excluded. Its per-arm figures appear only inside a report that pools it with a trial this object already holds separately, and that report is behind a paywall. No paywall was bypassed.

studies.registration_note: No registration for this trial was found in ClinicalTrials.gov; it ran before registration became a condition of publication.
studies.reason_no_data: the accessible record publishes its clinical cure figures only POOLED with study 3074A1-301, which this object holds as a separate row. Adding the pooled figure would count that trial twice.
studies.what_would_be_needed: the per-trial table of the pooled report, or a separate publication of this trial's own arms.
studies.arithmetic_deliberately_not_done: Subtracting the held trial's evaluable counts from the pooled ones would produce a number for this trial. It is not done, because it assumes the pooled report reproduced the held trial's evaluable counts exactly, and that assumption cannot be checked against a report this build cannot read. An unverifiable assumption dressed as arithmetic is the failure this batch exists to prevent.

methodological_authority.reference: Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al (editors). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1. Cochrane, 2025.
methodological_authority.version_checked_how: The publisher's versions-and-changes page was read, and it is what settles which version is current: it lists 6.5.1 as the newest release line, with entries dated 2026 and 2025, above 6.5 dated 2024. Each chapter relied on was then opened and its own printed citation line read; the table below is what those lines say. Two of the publisher's pages disagree and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved in silence: the Handbook landing page and the current-version index both still print version 6.5 updated August 2024. Where they conflict this object follows the version history and the per-chapter citation lines, because those are the more specific and the more recent statements.

chapters_as_dated_by_the_publisher.title: Defining the criteria for including studies

methodological_authority.version_note: The Handbook is versioned as a whole AND dated per chapter, and the two do not move together: the table above gives each chapter the version and the last-updated date the publisher prints on it, and they are not the same as each other. Listing them chapter by chapter keeps the age of the authority behind each decision visible instead of averaged away.
methodological_authority.note: Every scope, measure, population and pooling decision names the section governing it, on the block it governs.

sections_relied_on.title: Defining types of participants: which people and populations?
sections_relied_on.used_for: The restriction to one indication. The section asks for criteria broad enough to cover the likely diversity of studies but narrow enough that a meaningful answer is obtained when the studies are considered together, and names the definition of the condition as a consideration.

sections_relied_on.title: Defining which comparisons will be made
sections_relied_on.used_for: The restriction to one comparator. A trial against a different active drug is a different comparison, not another instance of this one.

sections_relied_on.title: Studies (not reports) as the unit of interest
sections_relied_on.used_for: Why a report that pools two trials is not a source for either trial's own arms, and why using it beside a trial already held would double count.

sections_relied_on.title: A typical process for selecting studies
sections_relied_on.checked_because_disputed: A judge leg said this sentence belongs to 3.2.4 and not here. The chapter was opened: 4.6.3 contains, verbatim, 'Note that studies should not be omitted from a review solely on the basis of measured outcome data not being reported', with its MECIR box beside it. That leg also gave 3.2.4 the title 'Defining outcomes'; its actual title is 'Selecting, prioritizing and grouping review outcomes'. The citation stands, and 3.2.4 is cited separately for what it does govern here, which is the outcome's time frame.
sections_relied_on.used_for: The disposition of the eligible trial whose own figures are unavailable: the section forbids omitting a study solely because its outcome data are unreported, so it is held rather than excluded.

sections_relied_on.title: Selecting, prioritizing and grouping review outcomes
sections_relied_on.used_for: The outcome's TIME FRAME. The section says reviews commonly specify a time frame rather than a specific time point precisely to handle diversity in the timing of measurement across studies, and the expectation printed with it asks that no more than one time point be taken from any study for an outcome. Both are what this pool does, and it is why the differing test-of-cure intervals are declared rather than described as identical.

sections_relied_on.title: Which effect measure for dichotomous outcomes?
sections_relied_on.used_for: The choice of the risk ratio, the requirement to make a sensible and declared choice of which category is the event, and the section's own warning that choosing a measure BECAUSE it is the most consistent is not a recommended strategy.

sections_relied_on.title: What is heterogeneity?
sections_relied_on.used_for: Clinical and methodological diversity across the pooled trials is documented rather than treated as disqualifying.

sections_relied_on.title: Identifying and measuring heterogeneity
sections_relied_on.used_for: The band the observed inconsistency falls in, reported beside the pooled line.

sections_relied_on.title: Types of missing data
sections_relied_on.used_for: Participants excluded from an evaluable population are missing individuals, and the expectation printed with that section asks authors to follow intention-to-treat principles as far as possible. It is why the evaluable population is declared as a limitation and tested.

sections_relied_on.title: Incorporating heterogeneity into random-effects models
sections_relied_on.used_for: The choice of a random-effects model AND of the estimator for the between-study variance, which the effect-measure sections do not govern. Its subsections carry the record that other estimators perform better than the one kept here, and the advice to compare methods when there are only two or three studies.

sections_relied_on.title: Sensitivity analyses
sections_relied_on.used_for: Testing whether the finding is robust to the decisions taken in reaching it.

cure_toc_me.derivation: The registry posts this outcome as PERCENTAGES over posted denominators, not as counts. The posted category Cure gives 88.0 per cent over 125 participants for tigecycline and 95.3 per cent over 107 for imipenem/cilastatin. 0.880 x 125 = 110 exactly. 0.953 x 107 = 101.97, which rounds to 102, and 102 of 107 is 95.327 per cent, which prints as the posted 95.3. Both counts are therefore determined by the posted figures rather than chosen. A separate registry outcome on the same record, MICROBIOLOGICAL response in the same population, happens to carry the same two percentages over the same two denominators; the clinical row here is taken from the CLINICAL outcome, and the coincidence is stated so a reader can check that it was not lifted from the microbiological one.

handbook.decision: POOL the three trials that share indication, comparator, outcome and analysis population, on the risk ratio of cure, by random effects; and report in the same breath that the exclusion of the null does not survive the alternatives the Handbook asks to be tested
handbook.conformance: Section 10.4.3 recommends that meta-analyses be undertaken using risk ratios or odds ratios and asks for a sensible, declared choice of which category is the event; the risk ratio of cure is used and the event category is declared on the outcome. That section also warns that selecting an effect measure BECAUSE it is the most consistent is not a recommended strategy, since it can spuriously maximise precision, and this object is bound by that warning: the risk ratio is not chosen for its lower inconsistency, it is chosen as one of the two measures the section recommends and on its ease of interpretation, which the same section discusses. The odds ratio is reported beside it. What the pooled trials differ in is recorded under 10.10.1 rather than treated as disqualifying, and the inconsistency statistic is reported in the bands of 10.10.2. Section 10.14, with 10.4.3's own instruction to test the choice of statistic and of event category, is why the sensitivity block exists and why its result is reported as prominently as the primary line. Section 10.10.4 is what governs the MODEL and the estimator, which the effect-measure sections do not: it records that estimators other than DerSimonian and Laird perform better and that restricted maximum likelihood is now the default in the Cochrane software, and its subsection on few studies advises comparing the methods when there are only two or three. That comparison is in the sensitivity block, on all three estimators and on both interval methods.

indication: every pooled trial states complicated intra-abdominal infection as its indication: 'patients with cIAI randomly received intravenous (IV) tigecycline ... or IV IMI/CIS', 'Chinese patients with cIAIs', and a phase four study in 'Hospitalized cIAI patients'.
comparator: every pooled trial randomises against imipenem/cilastatin by name, in the design sentences quoted for each on its own row.
outcome: every pooled trial reports clinical cure at the test-of-cure visit; the differing WINDOW of that visit is recorded as its own dimension below rather than folded into this one.
analysis_population: every pooled row is the MICROBIOLOGICALLY EVALUABLE population: 'For the ME group, clinical cure rates at TOC were 80.6% (199/247)', 'In the microbiologically evaluable population, 86.5% (45 of 52)', and the registry's posted 'Clinical Response at the TOC Assessment Within the Microbiologically Evaluable (ME) Population'. An earlier version declared this identical with nothing behind it, which a build-time rule added after the malaria comparator defect now refuses.
blinding: two trials are double-blind and one is open-label. An open-label trial of a subjective, investigator-assessed outcome is the more susceptible to assessment bias, and its removal is one of the leave-one-out analyses
test_of_cure_window: each protocol defines its own test-of-cure interval and the three do not coincide: one runs fourteen to thirty-five days after therapy, one twelve to thirty-seven, and one fourteen to twenty-one days after the last dose. Section 3.2.4 is what permits this and what it asks for: it says a review commonly specifies a time FRAME rather than a specific time point precisely to handle diversity in timing across studies, and its expectation on predefining time points asks that no more than one time point be taken from each study for an outcome, which is what happens here. An earlier version of this table called the outcome identical without qualification, which made the windows look the same; a reviewer read the three protocols and found they are not
region: one trial is multinational and two enrolled in one country
trial_size: the evaluable populations differ by roughly an order of magnitude between the largest and the smallest, so the smallest contributes little weight but can still move a random-effects estimate

between_study_variance_method_comparison.why: Section 10.10.4.4 records that other estimators of the between-study variance perform better than DerSimonian and Laird and that the restricted maximum likelihood method is now the default in the Cochrane software, and section 10.10.4.5 advises in terms that with only two or three studies the different methods should be compared in a sensitivity analysis. This pool has three, so the comparison is done rather than the advice merely cited.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.sections_checked_because_disputed: A judge leg said this guidance lives in 10.10.4.1, titled 'Between-study variance estimators'. It does not. The chapter was opened: 10.10.4.1 is 'Fixed or random effects?'. The restricted maximum likelihood and RevMan-default text is in 10.10.4.4, 'Implementing random-effects meta-analyses', and the advice to compare methods with two or three studies is the closing sentence of 10.10.4.5. Both are quoted in this object's own authority registry. The citations stand.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.verdict: The three variance estimators agree closely, which is what the Handbook reports is usual: they can differ substantially in the heterogeneity they estimate but seldom move the summary effect much. The interval method is what matters here. Under the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval the null is no longer excluded, and section 10.10.4.5 says exactly what to make of that: with three studies that interval is likely to be too wide, while the ordinary one is likely to be too narrow, so neither is taken as decisive and both are shown.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.estimator_kept: The headline estimator is restricted maximum likelihood, which is what section 10.10.4.4 records as the default in the Cochrane software and the direction its evidence points: it says in terms that other methods for estimating the between-study variance perform better than DerSimonian and Laird. An earlier version of this object kept DerSimonian and Laird as the headline and gave as its reason that the local validator could recompute it. A reviewer was right that this is not a methodological reason at all, and that it mattered here, because the headline is the line that excludes the null. The tooling was the thing that had to move, not the method: the validator now recomputes restricted maximum likelihood independently, so the Handbook's default and external checkability are no longer in tension. DerSimonian and Laird is still shown beside it, and it makes almost no difference to the summary, which is what the Handbook says to expect.

sensitivity.conclusion: The DIRECTION is stable: every trial's point estimate, every alternative statistic and every leave-one-out set puts tigecycline below its comparator on cure. What is NOT stable is the exclusion of the null. It survives only under the risk ratio of cure, on the evaluable population, with all three trials in. Reporting the primary line without this block would present a fragile result as a firm one.

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.estimator: REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 2 degree(s) of freedom (t = 4.3027)
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.THE_POINT_ESTIMATE_IS_UNCHANGED: The published point is 0.9351 and the house-rule point is 0.9351. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.variance_inflation_floor: A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.no_rule_is_decided_here: The house rule is REML with Hartung-Knapp below k=10, settled days ago. Whether it means ALWAYS or WITH A FLOOR AT k=3 is a decision about this corpus, not a computation, and it has been referred rather than taken. BOTH INTERVALS STAND ON THIS PAGE UNTIL IT IS MADE. Nothing is unpublished and no reader is left with only the narrower one.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.what_this_means_for_this_pool: THE PUBLISHED INTERVAL EXCLUDES 1 AND THE HOUSE-RULE INTERVAL CROSSES IT. A SIGNIFICANCE VERDICT TURNS ON THE INTERVAL METHOD ALONE. A reader shown only the published interval has been told something firmer than the evidence supports; a reader shown only the wider one loses that the contributing trials agree. BOTH ARE HERE.

cure_toc_me.estimand_established_does_not_cover_the_: READ THIS BESIDE `estimand_established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the SAME QUANTITY. It records NOTHING about what that quantity was measured AGAINST -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. On attr-pn-review the flag is TRUE and correct while the pool combines patisiran against its own saline placebo, vutrisiran against PATISIRAN, and eplontersen against the placebo cohort of a DIFFERENT TRIAL. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.

POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_this_pool_crosses_analysis_populations: THE ANALYSIS POPULATION IS PART OF THE ESTIMAND AND THIS POOL CROSSES IT. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT00081744 registers 'NO PRIMARY OUTCOME IS RECORDED ON THIS REGISTRATION' (population: NONE RECORDED); NCT00136201 registers 'Clinical response for all microbiologically evaluable and microbiologically modified intent-to-treat subjects' (population: ME and m-mITT); NCT01721408 registers 'Clinical Response at the Test-of-Cure (TOC) Assessment Within the Clinically Evaluable (CE) Population' (population: CE). The populations pooled are CE and ME and m-mITT.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_why_that_matters: A CLINICALLY EVALUABLE population EXCLUDES protocol violators and indeterminate responses, and microbiologically-defined populations exclude patients without a qualifying pathogen. Those are SELECTED SUBSETS of the modified intent-to-treat population and systematically yield HIGHER cure rates. A cure-rate ratio computed in one is not an estimate of the same quantity as one computed in another, so this pooled value depends on which trial registered which population.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.c_what_is_not_claimed: NOT that the arithmetic is wrong. NOT that the direction would reverse -- that would need the per-population counts and is NOT established. And NOT that these are non-inferiority trials: THE REGISTRATIONS FETCHED DO NOT USE THAT WORD, so the design question is unresolved from the registry rather than assumed.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_a_fifteen_study_network_finds_no_diffe: A PUBLISHED NETWORK META-ANALYSIS OF FIFTEEN STUDIES AND 6,745 PARTICIPANTS CONCLUDES: 'No differences in clinical and microbiological outcomes were observed between different carbapenems and TGC' (Yu et al., Medicine 2019, PMID 31577763). THIS POOL REPORTS RR 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842) ON THREE TRIALS -- an interval that excludes no difference, read as tigecycline being inferior on clinical cure.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_and_our_own_small_sample_correction_ag: THE INFERIORITY CONCLUSION DOES NOT SURVIVE THIS OBJECT'S OWN ADJUSTMENT. The Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3 is 0.8327 to 1.0501 on t = 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, and it INCLUDES no difference. A reader taking inferiority from this page is reading the unadjusted interval only.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.c_the_evidence_base_here_is_weaker_than_: One contributing trial is OPEN-LABEL (NCT00136201 registers masking NONE) on an assessed clinical-response endpoint; one registers NO PRIMARY OUTCOME AT ALL (NCT00081744, open item O0a) so its result cannot be checked against anything; and the three define their primary in DIFFERENT ANALYSIS POPULATIONS. GRADE certainty is VERY LOW.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.d_what_is_not_established: WHICH twelve studies the network carries that this object does not. The abstract names none and no included-study table was read, so the gap is COUNTED AND NOT IDENTIFIED.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.e_the_inferiority_reading_does_not_survi: READ THIS BEFORE THE INTERVAL ABOVE. The estimate is 0.9351 (0.8885 to 0.9842), which EXCLUDES no difference and reads as tigecycline being inferior on clinical cure. THIS PROJECT'S OWN HARTUNG-KNAPP INTERVAL AT k = 3 IS 0.8327 to 1.0501, on a t critical value of 4.3027 with 2 degrees of freedom, AND IT INCLUDES NO DIFFERENCE. The house rule already requires the adjusted interval to be shown beside the unadjusted one where k is small, because that is the honest width; on this pool the two disagree about the conclusion.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.f_and_a_fifteen_study_network_reached_th: Yu et al., Medicine 2019, PMID 31577763, a Bayesian network meta-analysis of FIFTEEN STUDIES and 6,745 participants, concluded: 'No differences in clinical and microbiological outcomes were observed between different carbapenems and TGC.' THE ADJUSTED INTERVAL AND THE LARGER LITERATURE AGREE WITH EACH OTHER AND NOT WITH THE UNADJUSTED READING.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.g_what_has_and_has_not_been_done: THE STORED ESTIMATE IS NOT CHANGED. Withdrawing or restating a published number is a content decision. What has been done is to put the adjusted interval and the disagreement where a reader meets the number, because a page that concludes more than its own stated method supports had been passing while pages that refuse honestly are marked incomplete.

SCOPE:indication-intra-abdominal-only.decision: Restrict to complicated intra-abdominal infection, and exclude the other licensed indication
SCOPE:indication-intra-abdominal-only.conformance: Section 3.2.1 asks for participant criteria broad enough to encompass the likely diversity of studies but narrow enough that a meaningful answer is obtained when the studies are considered together, and names the definition of the condition among the considerations. The two indications are different infections, treated at different sites, and in this drug's programme they were studied against DIFFERENT comparators, so combining them would answer neither question. The review this object replaces combined them.

SCOPE:comparator-imipenem-cilastatin-onl.decision: Restrict to trials whose control arm is imipenem/cilastatin
SCOPE:comparator-imipenem-cilastatin-onl.conformance: Section 3.2.3 distinguishes the comparisons a review makes, and a trial of this drug against a different active regimen is a different comparison rather than another instance of this one. Pooling across comparators would produce a summary against a mixture that no patient is offered. The excluded trial is named under excluded_by_scope so the boundary is visible.

SCOPE:pooled-report-not-a-source-for-one.decision: Hold the second registrational trial as eligible and contributing no data; do not reconstruct its arms
SCOPE:pooled-report-not-a-source-for-one.conformance: Section 4.6.1 makes the STUDY, not the report, the unit of interest, which is why using the pooled figure beside a study already held here would count that study twice. It does NOT say a pooled report can never be a source for a component trial's arms, and an earlier version of this text implied that; a review leg was right to call it stricter than the section. Had this report printed a per-trial breakdown it would be a perfectly good source for it. The barrier is that it does not, and that its full text is paywalled. Section 4.6.3 governs what then happens to the study: a completed but unreported study that clearly meets the eligibility criteria is recorded rather than dropped, and the same section states that a study should not be omitted solely because its measured outcome data are not reported. So it is held, visible, contributing nothing.

MEASURE:risk-ratio-of-cure.decision: Use the risk ratio with CURE as the event, and report the odds ratio and the risk ratio of failure beside it
MEASURE:risk-ratio-of-cure.conformance: Section 10.4.3 recommends risk ratios or odds ratios and asks for care over which category is classified as the event. Cure is chosen as the event because it is the outcome every source publishes and the one the trials were designed around, and the choice is declared on the outcome rather than left implicit. The same section warns that picking the measure that is most consistent can spuriously maximise precision, so the observed inconsistency is reported but is NOT the reason for the choice. Both alternatives the section names, the other statistic and the other event category, are computed and reported, which is what it says it may be wise to do.

POPULATION:microbiologically-evaluable.decision: Analyse the microbiologically evaluable population, and declare it as a departure from the randomised one
POPULATION:microbiologically-evaluable.conformance: It is the only population for which all three trials publish a MICROBIOLOGICALLY evaluable result for this outcome. An earlier version said one trial published no counts at all for any other population; that was false and a reviewer caught it. That trial's registry also posts a plain modified intention-to-treat clinical response, with counts, and those figures are recorded on the trial. What it does NOT publish is a MICROBIOLOGICAL modified intention-to-treat result, and that is the population the other two report -- so it cannot join the sensitivity analysis without combining a plain intention-to-treat population with two microbiological ones under a single label, which is the estimand error this object exists to avoid. Section 10.12.1 treats participants excluded from analysis as missing individuals, and the expectation printed with it asks authors to follow intention-to-treat principles as far as possible, so using an evaluable population is a real limitation and is stated as one rather than presented as neutral. Section 10.14 is why it is tested: the two trials that also publish the modified intention-to-treat population are re-pooled on that population in the sensitivity block, and the answer changes.

reconciliation.access_limitation: Both syntheses are OPEN ACCESS and both full texts were retrieved from PubMed Central and read, so the statements below are taken from methods sections and reference lists rather than from abstracts. An earlier version of this block said neither full text was retrievable. That was false, and it was false in the worst way available: no attempt had been made, while the PMC identifier for each sat in this object's own staged PubMed record. A reviewer read the staged record and found them. What remains genuinely unresolved is narrower and is stated below.

matches.item: Whether the networks INCLUDED the trials pooled here
matches.detail: For the carbapenem synthesis this is settled from its own text rather than inferred: it states that fifteen randomised trials were included and attaches the reference numbers of that set, and every trial pooled here carries a number inside it. So the syntheses and this object draw on the same trials for this comparison, and their far larger trial counts are scope rather than disagreement -- they answer which of many regimens is best, and this object answers one pairwise question. For the other synthesis all three appear in the reference list, which is evidence they were seen and not proof of inclusion, and it is left at that.
The network ranks clinical treatment success with imipenem/cilastatin ABOVE tigecycline. That is the direction this object finds directly, from the pairwise trials alone.

matches.item: Which analysis population, and it settles a question raised in review
matches.detail: The larger synthesis states its policy in its methods: it preferentially extracted a modified intention-to-treat population for clinical success where possible, and otherwise used the intention-to-treat population or the available data. That is exactly the BEST-AVAILABLE strategy this object runs as one of its two analysis-population sensitivity rows, and it was added only because a review leg argued that refusing it was stricter than the Handbook. A published synthesis in this indication doing the same thing is external support for that leg's objection, so it is recorded here rather than left as the object's own judgement call.

The network reports the regimens as not statistically distinguishable. This object's pooled interval does exclude the null, but its own sensitivity block shows that exclusion failing under the odds ratio, under the complementary event, under the other analysis population and on two of three leave-one-out sets. A network on the odds ratio scale finding no distinguishable difference is what this object's own odds-ratio row finds too, so the two agree on the point that matters most.
The larger of the two syntheses names the clinical success rate as its primary outcome, which is the outcome this object pools.
